nodes.label: go build (CmdBuild)
nodes.desc: runBuild drives compilation of a package into a static binary; the binary's real entry point is runtime.main, not the user's main.

nodes.label: buildssa (SSA backend)
nodes.desc: buildssa lowers the IR of each function into SSA form; ssacompile/compile.go then runs its ordered pass sequence (opt, lower, cse) that produces machine code.

nodes.label: runtime.main
nodes.desc: runtime.main first runs schedinit to bootstrap GC, allocators and allp, then calls newproc to launch the user's main function as goroutine g1.

nodes.label: newproc / newproc1
nodes.desc: newproc allocates a new g via newproc1 and hands it to runqput; every go statement costs a small allocation, not a thread.

nodes.label: G / M / P structs
nodes.desc: g (L471) is a goroutine, m (L615) an OS thread, p (L774) a scheduler context holding a local run queue; schedt (L936) holds the global queue and idle M/P pools.

nodes.label: schedule loop
nodes.desc: schedule calls findRunnable, then execute binds the M to the chosen G; when a G blocks or exits the thread falls straight back into this loop.

nodes.label: findRunnable
nodes.desc: findRunnable checks the P's runnext and local runq, the global run queue, GC mark workers, the netpoller, and finally stealWork on other Ps.

nodes.label: gopark / goready
nodes.desc: gopark parks the current G (setting _Gwaiting) and lets the M keep working; goready/read make it runnable again on some P's queue.

nodes.label: chansend / chanrecv
nodes.desc: chansend locks the hchan, hands the value directly to a waiting receiver or buffers it; when full it enqueues a sudog and parks the sender.

nodes.label: mcache (per-P cache)
nodes.desc: Each P owns an mcache of per-size-class spans; refill pulls a fresh span from the mcentral lists when the local free list runs dry.

nodes.label: mallocgc
nodes.desc: mallocgc routes tiny (<16B) objects to the tiny allocator, small objects to mcache spans, and large objects straight to the mheap.

nodes.label: gcStart cycle
nodes.desc: gcStart flips the world into _GCmark with a write barrier, spreads tricolor marking over background workers, then gcMarkDone leads to concurrent sweep.

edges.label: compiler lowers each function to SSA
allocates a G into a P's run queue
M asks for the next runnable G
local runq, global runq, steal, netpoll
M executes G on its P
blocked G parks, M loops back
full buffer parks sender on sendq
